I'm David Maguire. I have worked in financial services for around fifteen years and now work in data and
analytics in banking. I came into the industry straight from school, and built my academic grounding
alongside work, most recently through an MSc in Financial Services.

Over the past year I have been preparing a PhD proposal in quantitative finance. The question I keep
returning to is not whether a model looks good on a backtest, but whether it would survive on data it has
never seen, and whether a result is real or an artefact of how many things were tried. That shapes how I
work: state the hypothesis first, compare against a fair benchmark, and report nulls and corrections as
readily as positives. My [pilot experiments](quant-lab/index.qmd) include two of my own earlier results
that fairer re-tests overturned, and those corrections changed the direction of the
[proposal](phd/index.qmd).

## Where I need to grow

The proposal sits where quantitative finance meets AI, and I am deliberately strengthening the parts my
background covers least: financial econometrics and forecast evaluation, and the established
asset-pricing and forecasting literature, which I am working through from AJG-ranked journals. The
[core reading](phd/index.qmd#core-reading) is listed with the proposal.

## How this site was built

I use AI tools in building this site — for writing code, generating figures, and drafting prose —
working from my own research questions, design choices, and interpretation. That does not lower the bar
each entry has to clear: every number is computed and checked in code before it goes up, every model is
one I can derive and defend from first principles, and the judgement throughout — what to test, what it
means, and what to conclude — is mine. I use these tools deliberately and say so openly; they help me
build faster, but they do not stand in for the understanding this site exists to demonstrate.

Earlier and broader working, including an equation library, a machine-learning library and notes for a
previous version of the proposal, has been archived so the site stays focused on the current research.
